mainTopic: Did בית שמאי act on their own rulings? Proofs from רבי יוחנן החורני's moist olives and from רבי יהושע's fear of ruling on צרת הבת.
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's investigation into whether בית שמאי actually acted on their own rulings when they disagreed with בית הלל. It first finishes rejecting a proof about a widened water trough, since onlookers would think it was done just to get more water. Then it tells the story of רבי יוחנן החורני, a student of שמאי, who refused moist olives because he followed בית הלל's stricter rule about a barrel of olives needing a hole. The ברייתא praises him for always following בית הלל, and the גמרא reasons that this praise only makes sense if בית שמאי really did act on their own view. A second proof comes from רבי יהושע, who would not rule on צרת הבת because he was afraid. Instead he testified that great families descended from צרות produced כהנים גדולים. The גמרא explains that his fear makes sense: even though by his view the children of a צרה who did יבום are not ממזרים, they would still be פגום, as shown by a קל וחומר from an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול. Finally, the גמרא explains that רבי יהושע was really asked two questions, one about the צרות and one about their children. It begins matching his words to each question, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Widening the trough proves nothing: onlookers would think it was for more water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting an earlier proof. Widening the water trough was not a public act of following בית שמאי, because anyone watching would think it was done only to increase the water flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone watching would say: he is only doing this to get more water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off an earlier proof about a water trough that was widened. It says the act does not show a public break with בית הלל, since people would just think the goal was more water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof tried to show that בית שמאי openly acted on their own view. This line weakens that proof. The action looked completely ordinary, so nobody watching would see it as a halachic statement against בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who sees; an onlooker

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say בית שמאי never acted on their view. It only says this particular act cannot prove they did it openly, because it looked like an ordinary practical repair.

phrases.english: Someone watching would say:
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier discussion about a water trough that was widened.

phrases.english: it is to increase the water that he is doing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹאֶה אוֹמֵר: לְאַפּוֹשֵׁי מַיָּא הוּא דְּקָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the rejection of the previous proof (the trough), which was brought before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the widened water trough as evidence that בית שמאי openly acted on their rulings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The act looked like an ordinary practical repair to get more water, so it was not a visible halachic statement.

steps.title: A new source: רבי יוחנן החורני refuses moist olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new story. רבי אלעזר בר צדוק saw his teacher רבי יוחנן החורני living on dry bread and salt in a drought. His father sent olives, but the teacher saw they were moist and politely said he does not eat olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said: When I learned Torah with רבי יוחנן החורני, I saw him eating dry bread with salt in years of drought. I told my father, and he said: Bring him olives. I brought them. He saw they were moist and said to me: I do not eat olives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer its question by telling a story. This step only sets up the facts; the halachic point comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the olives were moist. Liquid on food can make it able to become טמא, so רבי יוחנן החורני worried about eating them. He did not want to embarrass the giver, so he simply said he does not eat olives.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; introduces a source brought as proof

steps.confusionAlert: He was not saying he dislikes olives. The refusal was about the moisture, which raised a concern about טומאה. Saying 'I do not eat olives' was a polite way to refuse.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
When I was learning Torah
with Rabbi Yochanan HaChorani,
phrases.notes: He was a student of בית שמאי, which is why his behavior matters for this question.

phrases.aramaic: רָאִיתִי שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל פַּת חֲרֵיבָה בְּמֶלַח
phrases.english: I saw that he would eat dry bread with salt
in years of drought.
I came and told my father,
he said to me: Bring him olives,
and I brought them to him.
He saw that they were moist,
phrases.notes: Liquid on food can make it able to become טמא, so the wetness worried him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: אֵין אֲנִי אוֹכֵל זֵיתִים.
phrases.english: he said to me: I do not eat olives.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the trough proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source to answer the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a student of בית שמאי acted according to בית שמאי's rulings in practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The eyewitness story of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק about רבי יוחנן החורני.

steps.title: The father's reply: the barrel had a hole that got plugged
steps.stepSummary: The father sends back an explanation. The barrel holding the olives had a hole, but sediment plugged it up, and that is why the olives were still moist.
steps.simpleTranslation: I came and told my father. He said to me: Go and tell him that the barrel had a hole, only the sediment plugged it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The father explains why the olives were wet and why that should not be a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a hole shows the owner did not want the olive juice to stay with the olives. Moisture that is not wanted does not make the food able to become טמא. So the wetness came only because the hole got clogged, not because the owner wanted the liquid there.

keyTerms.meaning: a barrel with a hole in it

phrases.english: I came and told my father.
He said to me: Go and tell him,
the barrel had a hole in it,
only the sediment plugged it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאתִי וְהוֹדַעְתִּי אֶת אַבָּא. אָמַר לִי: לֵךְ וֶאֱמוֹר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story, giving the father's answer to the teacher's refusal.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוחנן החורני was following בית שמאי's practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The father's message that the barrel had a hole that later got plugged.

steps.title: The משנה about barrels of preserved olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. בית שמאי say a barrel of preserved olives does not need a hole, and בית הלל say it does. Both agree that if a hole was made and sediment plugged it, the olives are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: A barrel of preserved olives: בית שמאי say it does not need to have a hole made in it. בית הלל say it does need a hole. And they agree that if a hole was made and the sediment plugged it, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה behind the father's message, which shows the halachic background of the story. The analysis of what this proves comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that olive juice does not make the olives able to become טמא, so no hole is needed. בית הלל are stricter and require a hole to show the juice is unwanted. Everyone agrees a plugged hole still counts, so the father's olives are fine even by בית הלל. That suggests רבי יוחנן החורני, a student of בית שמאי, was being careful like בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: needs to have a hole made
pure; not able to receive טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: In this case בית הלל are the stricter side, since they require a hole. Both sides agree a hole that later got plugged by sediment still works. The father's message meant the olives were טהור even by בית הלל's standard.
steps.confusionAlert: Here בית שמאי are the lenient side and בית הלל the strict side. That is the opposite of what beginners usually expect.
steps.whyThisMatters: A student of בית שמאי worried about something only בית הלל require. That is the data the גמרא will use to test whether בית שמאי's followers acted on their own rulings.

phrases.english: And we learned: A barrel of preserved olives,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין צְרִיכָה לִנָּקֵב.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: it does not need to have a hole made.
And Beit Hillel say: it does need to have a hole made.
And they agree that if a hole was made in it
and the sediment plugged it, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: חָבִית שֶׁל זֵיתִים מְגוּלְגָּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the משנה behind the father's message, explaining why a plugged hole makes the olives acceptable.
steps.raayaObject: What a student of בית שמאי was worried about, and whether his practice matched בית שמאי or בית הלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about barrels of preserved olives, with the dispute and the shared agreement about a plugged hole.

steps.title: The teacher always followed בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by praising רבי יוחנן החורני. Even though he was a student of שמאי, he always acted like בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though he was a student of שמאי, everything he did, he did only according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the story of רבי יוחנן החורני with one last line of praise. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why he would not eat the moist olives. He held like בית הלל, who say the barrel needs a hole, so he was worried the olives were טמא. The ברייתא presents this as something special about him, since he was a student of שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: all his actions, meaning his practical behavior
according to the words of בית הלל

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁתַּלְמִיד שַׁמַּאי הָיָה,
phrases.english: And even though he was a disciple of Shammai,
phrases.notes: This is still the ברייתא, talking about רבי יוחנן החורני from the olive story.

phrases.english: all his actions he did not do
except according to the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁתַּלְמִיד שַׁמַּאי הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא whose story was told in steps 2-4.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי acted on their own rulings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The closing line of the ברייתא about רבי יוחנן החורני

steps.title: His praise proves that בית שמאי did act on their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that praising him for following בית הלל only makes sense if בית שמאי really acted on their own rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say בית שמאי did act on their view, that is why he is praised. But if you say they did not act on it, what is so special about him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the line it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following בית הלל is only praiseworthy if his own teachers, בית שמאי, actually acted differently. If בית שמאי never acted on their view, everyone would follow בית הלל anyway, and there would be nothing to praise. So the line shows that בית שמאי did act on their opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense if you say...
they acted, meaning בית שמאי practiced their own ruling
his greatness, or what is special about him

steps.whatToRemember: The praise of רבי יוחנן החורני is used as proof that בית שמאי did act on their own rulings.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say they acted
phrases.notes: "They" means בית שמאי, acting on their own opinion.

phrases.english: that is his greatness.
But if you say they did not act
what is his greatness?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא עָשׂוּ הַיְינוּ רְבוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the line quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their rulings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The praise of רבי יוחנן החורני for following בית הלל even though he was a student of שמאי

steps.title: רבי יהושע is afraid to decide about צרת הבת
steps.stepSummary: A new source: רבי יהושע is asked about צרת הבת. He says it is a מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל, and he refuses to decide because he is afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי יהושע what the law is for צרת הבת. He said it is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. They asked whom the הלכה follows. He said: Why are you putting my head between two great mountains, between בית שמאי and בית הלל? I am afraid they will crush my skull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second proof with "תא שמע." It tells a story that it will analyze in a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that רבי יהושע says he is afraid. The גמרא will soon argue that this fear shows something about whether בית שמאי acted on their view.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear, which introduces a new proof
the co-wife of a man's daughter, in the case of יבום

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They asked Rabbi Yehoshua,
what is the law of the rival wife of a daughter?
phrases.notes: This is the main case of our פרק. His daughter is married to his brother, and the brother dies childless.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מַחְלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: He said to them: It is a dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
And the halakha follows whose words?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתֶּם מַכְנִיסִין רֹאשִׁי
phrases.english: He said to them: Why are you putting my head
between two great mountains,
between two great opposing sides,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
I fear lest they crush my skull.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, separate proof on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי acted on their rulings
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's fearful answer about צרת הבת

steps.title: רבי יהושע testifies about two families from צרות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע does not give a ruling. Instead, he testifies that two great families in ירושלים came from צרות and included כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I testify to you about two great families in ירושלים: the בית צבועים family from בן עכמאי and the בית קופאי family from בן מקושש. They were children of צרות, and some of them were כהנים גדולים who served on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע continues his answer. He gives a historical testimony instead of a direct ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These families came from צרות who married other men, which follows בית הלל. If such children could become כהנים גדולים and serve on the מזבח, their status was accepted as fully valid. So his testimony quietly supports בית הלל without him openly ruling.

phrases.english: But I testify to you

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁתֵּי מִשְׁפָּחוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: about two great families that were in Jerusalem,
the Beit Tzevo'im family from Ben Akhmai,
phrases.notes: בן עכמאי and בן מקושש are the places these families came from.

phrases.english: and the Beit Kofai family from Ben Mekoshesh,
that they were children of rival wives,
and from them came High Priests,
and they served on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֲנִי מֵעִיד לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהושע's answer from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The accepted practice regarding children of צרות
steps.raayaSupportSource: Testimony about the families of בית צבועים and בית קופאי

steps.title: His fear proves that בית שמאי acted on their view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי יהושע's fear makes sense only if בית שמאי actually acted on their ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say בית שמאי acted on their view, that explains why he said "I am afraid." But if you say they did not act on it, why did he say "I am afraid"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its proof from the words "מתיירא אני" in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי really practiced their view, a clear ruling would have serious real-life results. Some children would be called ממזרים, and their families could turn against him. If בית שמאי never practiced their view, there would be nothing to be afraid of.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say they acted
that is why he said: I am afraid.
But if you say they did not act,
why did he say: I am afraid?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא עָשׂוּ הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר מִתְיָירֵא אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the story in steps 7-8.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי acted on their rulings

steps.title: Even if they acted, why would he be afraid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions its own proof. Even if בית שמאי did act on their view, it is still not clear why רבי יהושע should be afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if they did act, why "I am afraid"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning it just used. It sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the fear making sense only if בית שמאי acted. Now the גמרא asks why even that would be frightening, since the danger was supposed to be that children would be declared ממזרים. The next step explains why, by רבי יהושע's own view, that danger seems not to exist.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about the law of צרת הבת. It is a challenge to the proof from step 9, asking whether the fear really shows anything.

phrases.english: And even granting that they acted,
what is the meaning of "I am afraid"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְהִי נָמֵי דְּעָשׂוּ, מַאי מִתְיָירֵא אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of the proof in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from רבי יהושע's fear in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if בית שמאי acted on their view, the feared result, children being declared ממזרים, would not happen by רבי יהושע's own rule (step 11). So the fear seems to have no basis.

steps.title: But רבי יהושע holds the children are not ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: by רבי יהושע's own view, the children of צרות would not be ממזרים, so why be afraid?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהושע himself said that a ממזר comes only from a union punished by a court death penalty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the question from the last step. It shows why רבי יהושע's fear seems strange based on his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the הלכה follows בית הלל, a צרה who did יבום (as בית שמאי allow) is living with her husband's brother. That is a כרת-level sin, not a court death penalty. For רבי יהושע, a child from such a union would not be a ממזר, so there seems to be nothing for him to fear.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union who may not marry into the community
Sins punished by a death penalty carried out by a court
But didn't he say! (a challenge from someone's own words)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua say:
there is no mamzer except
from those liable to court-imposed death penalties!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge opened in step 10 by giving its source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהושע had reason to fear
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By his own view, children of צרות are not ממזרים, so nothing bad would come out of his testimony.

steps.title: Not a ממזר, but still פגום
steps.stepSummary: Even if the child is not a ממזר, he is still פגום, meaning unfit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he is not a ממזר, but at least he is flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. There was still something to fear, because the child would be פגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer lowers the level of the problem without removing it. The child born from a צרה who did יבום is not a ממזר, but he is disqualified from כהונה. A ruling like that would still hurt the families who had acted like בית שמאי, so the fear was real.

keyTerms.meaning: Flawed in lineage, unfit for כהונה

phrases.english: Granted, he is not a mamzer,
at least he is flawed.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי נָמֵי דְּמַמְזֵר לָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession: grants the point but finds a lesser problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the child is not a ממזר, there is nothing at stake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The child is still פגום, so the fear was real.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from an אלמנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the child is פגום using a קל וחומר from the son of an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אלמנה is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, and still her son from him is פגום. A צרה is forbidden to everyone, so surely her son is פגום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer that the child is פגום. It uses a קל וחומר, a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, a narrow prohibition, and yet her son from him is פגום. According to בית הלל, a צרה who did יבום falls under the prohibition of אשת אח, which applies to everyone. If the narrow prohibition makes the child פגום, the wider one surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול

phrases.english: By a kal vachomer from a widow:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַלְמָנָה, שֶׁאֵין אִיסּוּרָהּ נוֹהֵג בַּכֹּל —
phrases.english: Just as a widow, whose prohibition does not apply to everyone —
phrases.notes: She is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, not to other men.

phrases.english: her son is flawed,
this one, whose prohibition is equal for everyone, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the obvious ending: all the more so her son is פגום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר מֵאַלְמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The son of a צרה who married without חליצה is פגום
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from the son of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's fear makes sense. Even without ממזרות, a ruling like בית הלל would make the children of צרות who did יבום (following בית שמאי) פגום, unfit for כהונה.

steps.title: Asked about צרות, answered about their children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יהושע's answer does not match the question he was asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked him about the צרות, and he answers them about the children of צרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the story. The question was about the צרות, but his testimony was about their children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was about צרת הבת herself: does she need יבום or חליצה? רבי יהושע's testimony was about families who came from צרות, meaning children. So his reply seems to miss the question.

phrases.english: They asked him about rival wives,
and he answers them about the children of rival wives!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָבְעוּ מִינֵּיהּ צָרוֹת, וְקָפָשֵׁיט לֵיהּ בְּנֵי צָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side issue about the story from steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The match between the question asked and רבי יהושע's testimony
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An answer about children does not answer a question about the mothers.

steps.title: He was really asked two questions
steps.stepSummary: There were two questions. The first was about the צרות. The second was about the children of צרות according to בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked him two things. First, what is the law for צרות? Second, if the law follows בית הלל, what do בית שמאי say about the children of צרות who married following בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. The question had two parts, and רבי יהושע's testimony answers the second part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was about the צרה herself. The second asked how בית שמאי view children born when a צרה married someone else without חליצה, following בית הלל. His testimony about families with כהנים גדולים speaks to that second question.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say, if you decide

phrases.english: They were asking him two things:
What is the law of rival wives?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר צָרוֹת כְּבֵית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: And if you say rival wives follow Beit Hillel,
phrases.notes: That is, the צרות are exempt, and they may marry others without חליצה.

phrases.english: children of rival wives who acted by Beit Hillel —
what is their status according to Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי קָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the question as having two parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He was asked only about the צרות, so his answer about children missed the point.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was also asked about the children according to בית שמאי, and his testimony answers that.

steps.title: Why does the second question matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the second question makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why anyone would care how בית שמאי view these children if the law follows בית הלל. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we already rule like בית הלל, the opinion of בית שמאי seems to have no practical use. The גמרא wants to know what real question this helps settle.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the second question from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical use of knowing בית שמאי's view on children of צרות

steps.title: It helps settle the child of a man who remarries his divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The answer helps settle the status of a child born when a man remarries his divorcée, according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It helps us decide, according to בית הלל, about a child born to a man who took back his divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical point. The answer about children of צרות can be carried over to another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other case is a man who remarries his divorcée after she was married to someone else. The question there is whether their child is fit for כהונה, according to בית הלל. Knowing how a forbidden union affects a child in the case of צרות helps decide this similar case.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes back his divorced wife after she married another man

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a question asked in the name of בית שמאי can still teach us הלכה, because it settles a case that בית הלל also need to decide.

phrases.english: To resolve the status of the child
of one who remarries his divorcée, according to Beit Hillel.
phrases.notes: The question is whether that child is fit for כהונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִיפְשַׁט וְלַד מַחֲזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ לְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second question helps decide whether the child of a man who remarried his divorcée is פגום according to בית הלל.

steps.title: First side of the question: a קל וחומר says the child is flawed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the first side of the second question. Perhaps we say a קל וחומר: an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול is forbidden only to some men, yet her son is פגום. So this woman, who is forbidden to everyone, should surely have a son who is פגום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say a קל וחומר? An אלמנה married to a כהן גדול is not forbidden to everyone, and still her son is flawed. This woman is forbidden to everyone, so isn't it logical that her son is flawed too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining exactly what the second question was. This is the side that says the child should be פגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, yet a son from that union is פגום for כהונה. The woman in our case is forbidden more widely, to everyone. So if the lighter prohibition produces a flawed son, the wider one should too.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? This opens one side of a doubt.
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one.
A widow married to a כהן גדול, which is forbidden.
Flawed in lineage, disqualified from כהונה.

phrases.english: Do we say a kal vachomer:
And just as a widow married to a High Priest,
whose prohibition does not apply equally to everyone,
her son is flawed;
this one, whose prohibition applies equally to everyone,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the woman whose status is being asked about here.

phrases.english: is it not logical that her son is flawed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָאָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the second question, whose practical difference was given in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the קל וחומר from an אלמנה married to a כהן גדול make this child פגום?

steps.title: Second side: the קל וחומר can be refuted
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps the קל וחומר fails. An אלמנה is different, because she herself becomes a חללה. The woman in our case does not become disqualified herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe we can knock down this reasoning: an אלמנה is different, since she herself becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the doubt. It suggests the קל וחומר does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the lighter case is lighter in every way. Here the אלמנה is stricter in one way: she herself becomes a חללה. So maybe her son is flawed for that reason, and the woman in our case, who is not disqualified herself, would not pass that flaw to her son.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the other side of a doubt.
To refute or knock down an argument.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. It is only the second side of the question. The question is a doubt with two possible answers.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it can be refuted:
What about a widow, who herself becomes disqualified?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side to the קל וחומר proposed in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from אלמנה לכהן גדול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The אלמנה is stricter in one way, because she herself becomes a חללה, so she is not purely the lighter case.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's answer to the first question: I am afraid to rule on the צרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts showing that רבי יהושע did answer both questions. To the first question, about the צרות themselves, he said: I am afraid to rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to them: about the צרות, I am afraid to decide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts matching רבי יהושע's words to the two questions. This line is his answer to the first question, about the צרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the גמרא complained that his answer did not match the question. Now it shows that part of his reply, 'I am afraid,' answers the question about the צרות. The answer to the second question, about the children, continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: I am afraid, meaning he would not give a ruling.

phrases.english: And he said to them: about rival wives, I am afraid [to rule],

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ צָרוֹת מִתְיָירֵא אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After spelling out the second question, the גמרא goes back to רבי יהושע's reply and matches its first part to the first question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting רבי יהושע's reply into answers for two separate questions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His answer did not fit the question he was asked.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'I am afraid' answers the question about the צרות. The rest of his reply answers the question about their children.
